actions.action: Fertilise once a month in spring and summer with diluted fertiliser, every six weeks in colder months
If over-fertilised, stop fertilising and let a few waterings flush the soil
Check that the top third of the soil is dry before watering
Water lightly when the soil is dry
Inspect leaves for edema and the soil for oversaturation
Check pot drainage and make extra drainage holes
Place the pot on a saucer
In extreme cases, repot in better-draining soil
Move the plant to a brighter position with indirect light
If the space is shaded or in winter, get a grow light
Move the plant away from cold draughts, open windows and AC vents
If the plant can't be moved, protect it with gardening fleece

verdict.reason: This generic care list names overwatering as only one of five possible causes, buries the watering fix among many others, and never mentions natural die-off of older leaves or adding a pole; nothing in it is clearly harmful.
